title: Deadline Closure for the Acquisition Chain — conformance vectors

constants.source: RFC-0001 (task set, jitter, ceiling) and RFC-0008 §4a (residual)

provenance: Derived from the admission test in RFC-0008 §2, evaluated in integer arithmetic. Every figure traces to a published measurement or to the difference of two of them; none is invented for this file.

valid_vectors.name: canonical_250sps
valid_vectors.note: the canonical rate; RFC-0001 records this task set at U = 0.174

boundary_vectors.name: utilisation_exactly_at_ceiling
boundary_vectors.note: equality is admitted: the ceiling is 'may occupy at most', not 'below'

boundary_vectors.name: utilisation_below_ppm_resolution
boundary_vectors.note: Three nanoseconds past the exact ceiling and still admitted, because integer ppm cannot see it. Pinned deliberately: the resolution of the test is part of the test, and an implementation that silently used floating point would differ here.

boundary_vectors.name: utilisation_one_ppm_over
boundary_vectors.note: The smallest refusable overrun, and it is four nanoseconds rather than one: utilisation is computed in parts per million and one ppm of a 4 ms period is 4 ns, so the test cannot resolve finer. An implementation that refuses at 1_000_001 ns is using different arithmetic and will disagree with this one somewhere it matters.

boundary_vectors.name: response_exactly_fills_period
boundary_vectors.note: R == D is admitted; the deadline is 'must finish before the next sample arrives', and arriving exactly then has finished The ceiling is relaxed to 100% in this case so that the deadline is the only thing being tested; a vector that omits an input it depends on cannot be re-derived, which is how this file's own checker caught it.

boundary_vectors.name: response_one_ns_over_period
boundary_vectors.note: one nanosecond past the period is a missed deadline The ceiling is relaxed to 100% in this case so that the deadline is the only thing being tested; a vector that omits an input it depends on cannot be re-derived, which is how this file's own checker caught it.

boundary_vectors.name: zero_blocking_declared
boundary_vectors.note: RFC-0008 N3: a term set to zero must still be declared. An implementation with no argument for it cannot express this case

rejection_vectors.name: 500sps_over_ceiling
rejection_vectors.note: the deadline itself is met; the published ceiling refuses it. An implementation that admits this has no ceiling, or a different one

rejection_vectors.name: 1000sps_over_ceiling
rejection_vectors.note: the deadline itself is met; the published ceiling refuses it. An implementation that admits this has no ceiling, or a different one

rejection_vectors.name: 2000sps_deadline
rejection_vectors.note: the only row refused by the deadline rather than by the ceiling; reporting the others this way conflates two distinct refusals

rejection_vectors.name: rate_0_unsupported
rejection_vectors.note: a rate the front end cannot produce is refused, not approximated

rejection_vectors.name: rate_300_unsupported
rejection_vectors.note: a rate the front end cannot produce is refused, not approximated

rejection_vectors.note: a rate the front end cannot produce is refused, not approximated

rejection_vectors.name: rate_251_unsupported
rejection_vectors.note: a rate the front end cannot produce is refused, not approximated
